title: Shift compatibility of balanced derived scalar associators
statement: For a scalar presentation family p on an essentially r-small site and its balanced normalization n [def-pur-ringed-coefficient-projection-data, lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization], fix coherent integer shifts on every p(a).derived, normalized by shift compatibility of every universal counit. Then the given balanced derived comparison n.derived(a,b) commutes with shifts for each composable pair of coefficient maps a and b. No coefficient map is required to be flat and no complexes are assumed bounded.

source.place: Tags 0D6D and 07A6: balanced scalar associators and the normalized derived comparisons; universal Kan extension uniqueness.

proof.text: The ordinary balanced natural isomorphism maps termwise to cochain complexes with degreewise components. The termwise functor shift comparisons have identity components, so its shift equation follows by the component calculation. The homotopy quotient factorization isomorphisms transfer that equation to mapHomotopyCategoryCompIso.

Compose the two scalar universal counits and the termwise ordinary balanced comparison to get a natural transformation beta from Qh followed by the two derived scalar functors to the ordinary composite-map homotopy functor followed by Qh. Each factor commutes with shifts.

Lift beta through the right Kan extension counit of the derived composite-map scalar functor. Postcomposition by the shift equivalence preserves this Kan extension. Its uniqueness, applied to the two sides of the lift shift equation and the counit shift squares, proves compatibility of the universal lift with every shift.

On a flat-term K-flat representative, cancel the invertible composite-map counit. Its lift equation and the recorded normalization representative equation identify this lift with n.derived(a,b). Resolve every complex by flat-term K-flat complexes, invert the localization image of the augmentation, and use naturality to extend the equality to all Qh objects and hence all derived objects. Transfer the lift shift equation to the given balanced comparison.
